recordStatus: experimental — Clara's first Pattern Knowledge record; shape is a hypothesis to evaluate against Button/Input's component Knowledge shape, not a committed schema. See docs/knowledge/README.md for how and why this record's shape differs from a component record.

sourceOfTruth.implementation: none — no confirmation-surface component exists yet; this record is product/UX guidance only, not documentation of executable code
sourceOfTruth.explorerResult: app/src/App.tsx imports this JSON file directly (`import patternKnowledge from "../../docs/knowledge/destructive-confirmation.json"`) and renders its fields; App.tsx owns only presentation/formatting, not content — see docs/project/learning-log.md's H1 evidence entry

demonstratedIntent.value: I need users to confirm before deleting something.
demonstratedIntent.note: The exact example intent named in docs/slices/01-intent-first-discovery.md. This record, and the Explorer's deterministic result, resolve this one intent string — not a general class of destructive-action phrasing. See knownLimitations.

purpose.value: Help a consumer prevent a user from unintentionally or unknowingly executing an action that destroys, removes, or irreversibly changes something, by requiring an explicit, separate confirming step before it runs.
purpose.note: Proposed by this task's product-design analysis, not yet an approved Clara decision. Unlike button.json/input.json's purpose field, no existing Clara document states this in Clara's own words — it is reasoned from the demonstrated intent and general product-design analysis, not sourced from a prior decision.

value: The action destroys, removes, or irreversibly changes something a user would not want to lose by accident.
The action could be triggered by a single, low-friction interaction (one click/tap) without further review.
whenToUse.note: Reasoned from the demonstrated intent, not tested against a real product flow.

value: The action is cheaply and obviously reversible — an 'undo after the fact' pattern may be a better fit; see relatedPatterns.
The action is consequential but not destructive (e.g. publishing, sending) — a different review/confirmation pattern, not this one.

The destructive action is expected and high-frequency in the surrounding flow (e.g. a triage tool where delete is a primary verb) — confirming every time risks alert fatigue. No resolution is proposed for this case here.
whenNotToUse.note: Reasoned exclusions, not sourced from an explicit Clara decision and not tested against a real alternative flow.

value: Accidental, unrecoverable data loss.
A user executes a destructive action without understanding its scope, including cascading effects.
Loss of trust in the product after an unintended destructive action.
What specifically will be affected — named, not generic (e.g. 'Delete "Q3 report"?', not 'Are you sure?').
A consequence statement — irreversibility and scope, including cascading effects if any.
requiredContent.note: A heading alone ('Are you sure?') is judged insufficient by this analysis. Not tested against real users.

requiredActions.description: Aborts with no consequence. Must always be present and easy to reach.
Executes the destructive action. Requires a distinct activation step from whatever triggered the confirmation surface.

actionHierarchy.value: The non-destructive path (cancel) should be the easy/default path — e.g. default focus. The destructive path must be visually distinguishable as consequential, not styled identically to an ordinary primary action.
actionHierarchy.note: Whether the destructive action needs a new semantic role (e.g. color.action.danger) distinct from color.action.primary is explicitly unresolved — see unresolved. No such token exists in Clara today; docs/foundations/token-model.md already defers status/danger roles until a demonstrated need. This record does not create that need by itself — see composition and knownLimitations.

value: Reachable by keyboard (Escape, or a clearly focusable cancel control).
Dismiss-equivalents (clicking outside an overlay, browser back) behave as cancel, never as confirm.
Requires an explicit user activation distinct from the action that triggered the confirmation surface — never fires automatically.
Should not be triggerable by a keystroke a user might press habitually (e.g. Enter) unless focus was deliberately moved to it.
destructiveActionBehavior.note: Design goals, not verified guarantees — nothing exists yet to test either claim against.

composition.component: none — Clara has no Dialog/overlay component. Could be realized as a modal, an inline in-place replacement, a native confirm(), or avoided entirely via an undo-after pattern.
existing textStyle roles (heading / supporting / body) — no new typography needed
Clara Button — no secondary/ghost variant exists yet; button.json already records this as a known limitation
Clara Button — no destructive variant or semantic danger role exists yet

accessibility.claim: Focus should move to the confirmation surface (or its safe default action) when it appears.
The consequence text must be programmatically associated with the surface, not only visually adjacent, so it is announced by assistive technology.
The destructive signal must not rely on color alone — label wording (e.g. 'Delete') must carry the meaning too.

value: Reversible action / Undo-after — not built. A likely sibling or alternative resolution of the same underlying risk (protect against unintended destructive actions) using less friction. Whether this should be a separate Pattern or a branch of this one is unresolved.
Button (app/src/components/Button.tsx) — existing; no destructive or secondary variant

This record resolves exactly one demonstrated intent string via a deterministic match in the Explorer — not general search, not fuzzy matching, not AI matching. See docs/slices/01-intent-first-discovery.md, which explicitly permits this for a first experiment.
No confirmation-surface component exists — composition guidance is descriptive only, not executable.
No destructive/danger semantic token or Button variant exists — the Explorer's illustrative result reuses the existing action.primary Button styling for both actions, and says so.
Not validated against a second phrasing of the same intent, or against any other destructive-action intent.

unresolved: Whether destructive actions need a new semantic role (e.g. color.action.danger) distinct from action.primary — likely, but not demonstrated by this experiment.
Whether Clara needs a real Dialog/overlay component now, or should continue to defer it — this experiment deliberately does not build one.
Whether confirm-before and undo-after should be modeled as two separate Patterns or one Pattern with a branch.

Whether Pattern Knowledge should share button.json/input.json's status/origin shape as-is, or needs a lower epistemic ceiling (nothing here can reach 'observed' until something real composes it) and/or a third origin value distinguishing product/UX reasoning from web-platform fact — no origin field is applied anywhere in this record because no claim here traces to a web-platform fact; see docs/knowledge/README.md.

Whether the field shapes introduced here (requiredActions, composition, actionHierarchy, cancellationBehavior, destructiveActionBehavior, relatedPatterns) are reusable beyond this one Pattern record, or were only useful for this one record — same open question button.json/input.json already raised about their own experimental fields.
Whether Pattern should become a formal Clara system entity with its own repository-wide schema — explicitly not decided by this record; see docs/knowledge/README.md.
